body:
## Problem

AI coding agents working on this repo build each branch in its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (`target-<slice>`) and its own git worktree under `.claude/`. Nothing removes them after the branch merges. One developer machine reached 47 build folders, about 300 GB. It is also unclear which folders are safe to delete and what deleting them affects.

## Goal

A bounded, documented policy for build output during development:

1. **Fixed slots.** Agents reuse a fixed set of build folders (for example `target-w1`, `target-w2`, matching the limit of two parallel writers) instead of one new folder per branch. Incremental builds stay fast.
2. **Cleanup on merge.** A worktree and its build folder are removed when its PR merges.
3. **A cleanup script** (`scripts/clean-builds.sh`) that:
   - lists every build folder and worktree with its size, branch and merge state;
   - says what removing each one affects (only a rebuild, never source or uncommitted work);
   - refuses to touch a worktree with uncommitted changes;
   - removes the oldest merged ones above a size cap.
4. **Documentation** of this in `AGENTS.md`, so every agent follows it.

## Notes

Build folders only hold compiler output; removing them costs a rebuild and nothing else. Worktrees can hold uncommitted work and must be checked first.

comments.body:
Context from the first cleanup (2026-11-02), done by hand:

- 46 build folders (`target-*`) and 48 merged worktrees under `.claude/` were removed. Free space went from 255 GB to 531 GB, so about 276 GB.
- Before removing, every worktree was checked for uncommitted changes. All were clean except the one in active use, which was kept. Removal used `git worktree remove` without force, so a dirty one would have been refused. Branches were kept.
- Two build folders were kept: the one in use by a running agent, and `target-accept`, whose release binary was running at that moment.
- Lesson for the script: it must detect a running binary inside a build folder, not only uncommitted work, before removing anything.

title: chore: bounded build folders and worktrees for agents
